# Forms a verification library's run reaches

The task module runs every fixture through the public CLI in both HDL optimizer
modes on legacy, compact/portable and compact/GMP values; the generated-C sweep
(`tests/generated_c_frame_lint.rs`) compiles each one with `-Wall` and accepts
no warning. Expected outputs were checked against an independent
industry-standard simulator; the clause lines below are from
`SystemVerilog-1800-2009.txt`.

| Fixture | Clause and oracle |
| --- | --- |
| `unused_locals` | 6.21 L6901-6903: "Variables declared in an automatic task, function, or block are local in scope, default to the lifetime of the call or block and are initialized on each entry to the call or block". 8.6 L9766: "The lifetime of methods declared as part of a class type shall be automatic." String, class handle, chandle and process locals of class methods, automatic functions and an automatic task that nothing names after the declaration (a handle local beside a `$cast` destination, as in a library's `do_copy`); each call returns as if they were absent. |
| `wide_hierarchy_randomize` | 18.6.1 L30398-30399: "The randomize() method is a virtual function that generates random values for all the active random variables in the object, subject to the active constraints." 18.4 L29372-29373: "An object handle can be declared rand, in which case all of that object’s variables and constraints are solved concurrently with the variables and constraints of the object that contains the handle." A class with 40 derived classes (more than one dispatch chains) and a two-level chain under one of them, randomized through a base-class handle as a value, in an `if` condition and through a `rand` handle: the constraints of the object's own class hold. The task module also generates it without building and checks that the C nesting stays below the class count, so a class with hundreds of derived classes (a verification library's sequence items) stays within C compiler nesting limits. |
| `specialization_spellings` | 8.25 L10772-10776: "A specialization is the combination of a specific generic class with a unique set of parameters. Two sets of parameters shall be unique unless all parameters are the same as defined by the following rules: a) A parameter is a type parameter and the two types are matching types. ... All matching specializations of a particular generic class shall represent the same type." 8.25 L10754-10755: "Each specialization of a class has a separate set of static member variables". A type reaches `typeid #(T)` through two spellings (`typeid #(CB)` in one `callbacks` specialization, `typeid #(T)` in the next, and a typedef), as a library's `uvm_typeid #(CB)` and `uvm_typeid #(T)` do: each pair names one specialization with one singleton, and seven singletons exist. `generated_c_determinism` also generates the fixture six times per optimizer mode: the spelling the frontend keeps for a specialization depends on which reference reached it first, which changes between runs, so the class order must not depend on it. |
| `recursive_rand_handle` | 18.4 L29372-29374: "An object handle can be declared rand, in which case all of that object’s variables and constraints are solved concurrently with the variables and constraints of the object that contains the handle. Randomization shall not modify the actual object handle." A base class with a recursive `rand` handle and 13 derived classes (one of them two levels deep); a chain of six objects of five classes (two of the base class) linked through the handle, randomized three times through a base-class handle: every linked object meets its own class's constraints and the chain is unchanged. The industry-standard simulator gives the same output and also warns that the last object's handle is null. The task module also generates it without building, within a time bound, and checks that every unit links the handle once (`llg_cr_link` sites at most problems x units, 14 x 15), whatever the number of classes the child can have; before the class-to-unit table the fixture had 2940 link sites. |
| `string_format_time_unit` | 20.4.2 L34318-34320: "It specifies how the %t format specification reports time information for the $write, $display, $strobe, $monitor, $fwrite, $fdisplay, $fstrobe, and $fmonitor group of system tasks." 21.3.3 L36741-36742: "The $swrite family of tasks is based on the $fwrite family of tasks and accepts the same type of arguments as the tasks upon which it is based"; L36751: "$sformat supports all the format specifiers supported by $display". 21.2.1.2 L36105-36107: "The %t format specification works with the $timeformat system task to specify a uniform time unit, time precision, and format for reporting timing information from various modules that use different time units and precisions." Table 20-3 L34373: the default `units_number` is the smallest time precision. A module with unit 1 us and a package with unit 1 ns (precision 1 ps): `%t` of `$time`/`$realtime` through `$swrite`, `$sformat`, `$sformatf` and a run-time format gives the `$display` text, 1000000 (ps) by default and 1500 ns under `$timeformat(-9, 0, " ns", 5)`. |
| `string_function_packed_outputs` | 13.4 L18751-18755: "Functions can have the same formal arguments as tasks. Function argument directions are as follows: input // copy value in at beginning output // copy value out at end inout // copy in at beginning and out at end". A string-returning automatic function with a 1-bit output formal and a static string-returning function with an `int` inout and a 4-bit output formal, called as an assignment's right-hand side, inside concatenations and from a class method with class-property actuals: each actual holds the formal's final value after the call, and the static function's formals keep their storage between calls. The industry-standard simulator gives the same output. |
| `virtual_interface_type_parameter` | 25.9 L44897-44899: "The type of an interface shall include actual parameters, default or overridden, used in the instantiation of an interface or the declaration of a virtual interface variable. The actual values and types of those parameters shall match for an interface and virtual interface to be of the same type and to be assignment compatible". L44937-44938: "Virtual interfaces can be declared as class properties, which can be initialized procedurally or by an argument to new()." A class whose type parameter `T` is `virtual pins` stores an interface instance and a virtual interface variable through a `T` formal; writes through the property reach the instance. The type is spelled `holder::T` where the frontend meets it first, so the interface type must be identified by its interface, not by the first spelling. The industry-standard simulator gives the same output. |
| `virtual_interface_function_return` | 13.4 L18657: "The primary purpose of a function is to return a value that is to be used in an expression." 13.4 L18732: "To indicate the return type of a function, its declaration can either include an explicit data_type_or_void or use an implicit syntax". 25.9 L44919-44926: assignment of "Another virtual interface of the same type" and "An interface instance of the same type", and equality with either. A resource class parameterized on a parameterized virtual interface type, with and without a modport, stores interface instances in a static associative array; `function T read()` returns one, and a static `get` with an `inout T` formal copies it out to class properties; the driver then waits on and drives through them. The industry-standard simulator gives the same output. |
| `forward_class_typedef_in_module` | 6.18 L6029-6031: "Sometimes a user-defined type needs to be declared before the contents of the type have been defined. ... Support for this is provided by the following forms for a forward typedef: ... typedef class type_identifier;" L6046-6047: "The actual data type definition of a forward typedef declaration shall be resolved within the same local scope or generate block." Two `typedef class` declarations in a module, one class referring to a later one and two classes referring to each other: the forward declarations add nothing to run. The industry-standard simulator gives the same output. |
| `net_read_in_target_select` | 14.16 L20069-20071: "For each clocking block output whose target is a net, a driver on that net shall be created. The driver so created shall have (strong1, strong0) drive strength and shall be updated as if by a continuous assignment from a variable inside the clocking block." 10.4 L12967-12969: procedural assignments occur within procedures. Wires of an interface, driven by a clocking block, select the element, bit range and indexed range a slave module's nonblocking assignments write (`regs[bus.addr[1:0]][15:8] <= bus.wdata`): the nets are only read there, as a register-model example's slave reads its bus address. The industry-standard simulator gives the same output. |
| `duplicate_package_definition` (with `duplicate_package_definition_pkg.svh`) | 3.12.1 L2661-2667: "The exact mechanism for defining which files constitute a compilation unit is tool-specific. ... b) Each file is a separate compilation unit (in which case the declarations in each compilation-unit scope are accessible only within its corresponding file)." L2669-2670: "The contents of files included using one or more `include directives become part of the compilation unit of the file within which they are included." The header is passed as its own source and included again by the testbench: its include guard is not defined in the second compilation unit, so the package is defined twice (the frontend warns). A package-level associative array of class handles, filled through a function, holds one table: `a=1 b=2 c=1 created=2 entries=2`. The industry-standard simulator gives the same output for the single-unit form (one definition). |
| `process_self_static_initializer` | 9.7 L12612: "The self() function returns a handle to the current process, that is, a handle to the process making the call." 6.8 L5286-5288: static initializers run "before any initial or always procedures are started". Known issue (see `docs/known_issues.md`, "UVM example differences"): llg returns null in the two static initializers and a running process with a working random state in the initial procedure. The industry-standard simulator returns a running process in the initializers too: `static: null=0`, `static: status=RUNNING`, `static: replay=1` (and the same for `static2`), then the three `initial` lines. The expected output pins llg's current behaviour. |
| `class_pattern_covergroup_member` | 19.4 L32210-32212: "A covergroup declaration within a class is an embedded covergroup declaration. An embedded covergroup declaration declares an anonymous covergroup type and an instance variable of the anonymous type. The covergroup_identifier defines the name of the instance variable." 21.2.1.7 L36387-36388: "The %p format specifier may be used to print aggregate expressions such as unpacked structures, arrays, and unions. For unpacked structure data types, it shall print the value as an assignment pattern with named elements." A monitor class with two embedded covergroups between its properties, a derived class adding a third, and a module-level covergroup; a parameterized pool class prints its entries with `$swrite(v, "%p", p[k])`: the patterns name the properties and leave the covergroup instances out. The industry-standard simulator gives the same output. |
| `fixed_array_to_dynamic_handles` | 7.6 L8421-8424: "A fixed-size unpacked array, dynamic array or queue, or a slice of such an array, shall be assignment compatible with any other such array or slice if all the following conditions are satisfied: — The element types of source and target shall be equivalent." L8436-8441: "Assignment shall be done by assigning each element of the source array to the corresponding element of the target array. Correspondence between elements is determined by the left-to-right order of elements in each array. ... If the target of the assignment is a queue or dynamic array, it shall be resized to have the same number of elements as the source expression". Fixed arrays of class handles (a block-local one initialized from a pattern, a class property, one of nulls) and of strings (declared `[2]`, `[2:0]` and `[1:3]`) assigned to dynamic arrays, one of them first sized 5: each target takes the source's size and its elements in left-to-right order, and later writes to the source leave the copy unchanged. The industry-standard simulator gives the same output. |
| `assertion_bit_vector_functions` | 16.12 L24217-24222: "Assertions are commonly used to evaluate certain specific characteristics of a design implementation, such as whether a particular signal is “one-hot”. The following system functions are included to facilitate such common assertion functionality: — $onehot (<expression>) returns true if only 1 bit of the expression is high. — $onehot0 (<expression>) returns true if at most 1 bit of the expression is high. — $isunknown (<expression>) returns true if any bit of the expression is X or Z." 16.5 L21447: "All variables in a concurrent assertion use the value sampled in the Preponed region of a time slot". Assertions in a clocked procedure of an interface (with `disable iff`) and at module level use `$onehot`, `$onehot0`, `$countones` and `$isunknown` in antecedents and consequents: each fails at the clock where the sampled arguments break it (a write at the clock edge is seen at the next one), and nothing fails once the checks are disabled. The industry-standard simulator gives the same action-block output; it also prints its own failure reports, which the expected output leaves out. |
| `inline_constraint_receiver_path` | 18.7 L30539-30552: "The scope for resolution of variable names referenced in an unrestricted constraint block begins with the randomize() with object class; that is, the class of the object handle used in the method call to randomize. Then, if a name fails to resolve within the randomize() with object class, the name is resolved normally starting in the scope containing the inline constraint." 18.6.1 L30398-30399: "The randomize() method is a virtual function that generates random values for all the active random variables in the object, subject to the active constraints." `req`, `this.req` and `h.req` resolve in the caller, and each names the object being randomized, so `req.size`, `req.data.size()` and `h.req.addr` in the inline constraints are that object's random variables (a sequence's `uvm_do_with` constrains its item this way); `other.kind` and `other.size` name another object and read its values. The industry-standard simulator gives the same output. |
